text:
Assistant A attempts an actual proof, with the right structure: assume √2 = p/q in lowest terms, get p² = 2q², conclude p is even, and reach a contradiction. It has flaws. It runs to 14 lines, not fewer than 10, and says "10 line." It barely rhymes. Its descent argument is also muddled: it says "repeat the process" instead of noting that q must also be even, which contradicts lowest terms. Still, the mathematical content is mostly relevant and recognizable as a proof.

Assistant B is a poem with some rhyme, but it contains no proof at all. It also makes false or misleading claims, such as "always changing" and "we will never know." It has 10 lines, which does not satisfy "less than 10" either, and its rhyme is weak.

A is better on the core task of proving the statement, despite its formatting failures.
